sentences.text: Halisaurus auriculatus was described as a new species in 2026 in the journal Acta Palaeontologica Polonica.
The type locality for the species is the Dakhla Formation of Egypt, and all known specimens come from that country.
Halisaurus auriculatus is recognized as a valid mosasaur species.
It belongs to the subfamily Halisaurinae within the mosasaur family.
Phylogenetic analysis places it in a polytomy with H. hebae and the clade containing H. arambourgi and H. platyspondylus.
Halisaurus auriculatus lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
The broader genus Halisaurus persisted from the Santonian to the Danian, roughly 85.7 to 61.66 million years ago.
The coexistence of two morphologically distinct halisaurine species in the Dakhla Shale has been interpreted as possible niche partitioning among these mosasaurs.
